lines.japanese: 「ただいま」
lines.english: “I'm home.”

lines.japanese: 玄関のドアを開けて、誰に言うでもなく呟いた。
lines.english: I opened the front door and murmured the words to no one.

lines.japanese: 帰宅する僕を迎えたのは、照明さえ落ちた凍える廊下だ。
lines.english: I came home to a freezing hallway with even the lights turned off.

lines.japanese: 暗がりの中ドアを閉め、手探りで鍵をかけなおしていると、頭上、階段の先に細い光が漏れた。
lines.english: I shut the door in the darkness and felt around to lock it again. Then, overhead, a narrow thread of light escaped from the top of the stairs.

lines.japanese: そして、ほとんど音も立てずに、小さな足がそろそろと下りてくる。
lines.english: A pair of small feet began their cautious descent, scarcely making a sound.

lines.japanese: 小鳩だ。二階の彼女の部屋まで玄関の音が聞こえたんだろう。首を伸ばすようにしてこちらを窺っている。
lines.english: Kobato. She must have heard the front door from her room upstairs. She craned her neck and peered down at me.
“...Who's there?”

lines.japanese: 暗さのせいで僕の顔が見えてないみたいだ。まだ夜のお留守番が心細い年頃なのかもしれない。安心させるように声をかけた。
lines.english: The darkness seemed to hide my face. Perhaps she was still at an age when being left alone after nightfall frightened her. I spoke to reassure her.

lines.japanese: 「おれだよ。ただいま」
lines.english: “It's me. I'm home.”

lines.japanese: 「あ……おか、おかえりなさい」
lines.english: “Oh... W-welcome home.”

lines.japanese: 「ごめん、遅くなっちゃって」
lines.english: “Sorry I'm late.”

lines.japanese: 「んん、いい」
lines.english: “Mm-mm. It's fine.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩は硬い笑みを浮かべながら、首をふるふる横に振った。
lines.english: Kobato shook her head in quick little motions, a stiff smile on her face.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あの、ごはんとおふろ準備できてま……できてるから」
lines.english: “U-um, dinner and the bath have been prepa... They're ready.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう、ははっ」
lines.english: “Thank you. Haha.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩は僕と話してるときたまに、ポロッと方言みたいに敬語が出ちゃうんだ。家族なのに気を抜くと畏まっちゃうなんて、よそよそしいにも程がある。気付いてすぐ言いなおすのはちょっと可愛いんだけど。
lines.english: When Kobato talked to me, formal language sometimes slipped out as though it were her native dialect. We were family, yet the moment she relaxed, she grew formal. There were limits to how distant a person could be. The way she noticed and corrected herself at once was a little adorable, though.

lines.japanese: 僕はいったん廊下に背を向けて靴を脱ぐ。階段の板張りを踏みしめる音が、とんとん小気味よく遠ざかっていった。
lines.english: I turned my back on the hallway for a moment to remove my shoes. The crisp tap-tap of her feet on the wooden stairs receded overhead.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうだ小鳩、きのうのニュースどうだった？」
lines.english: “Oh, right, Kobato. How was that news story yesterday?”

lines.japanese: 「どうだったーじゃないわよ。お兄ちゃんってば、ほんっと呑気さんなんだから。ほら、宿題見てくれる約束だったでしょ、早くこっち来て！」
lines.english: “Don't you ‘how was it?’ me. Honestly, you haven't got a care in the world. You promised to help me with my homework, remember? Now hurry up and get over here!”

lines.japanese: 「お、おい、引っぱるなよ……ああ、こら、胸が当たってるって」
lines.english: “H-hey, don't pull… Wait, your chest is pressing against me.”

lines.japanese: 「え！？　きゃ、きゃあっ、お兄ちゃんのえっち！」
lines.english: “What?! Eek! You pervert!”

lines.japanese: という『ささやきマテリアル』にありそうな一幕を思いえがきながら、僕はひとり真っ暗な廊下の端で白い溜息を吐いた。
lines.english: Imagining a scene straight out of *Whisper Material*, I stood alone at the end of the pitch-dark hallway and sighed, my breath white in the cold.

lines.japanese: 階段の先を見上げれば、ばたんと閉ざされた小鳩の部屋からはすでに光すら漏れていなかった。
lines.english: I looked up the stairs. Kobato's door had slammed shut, and not even a thread of light escaped it now.

lines.japanese: 当たり前だ。誰だって用がなければ自分の居場所へ戻る。うちの子に限った話じゃない。みんなそうだ。きっとそうだ。
lines.english: Of course. Anyone with no reason to stay returned to the place where they belonged. It was not peculiar to the girl in our house. Everyone did it. Surely everyone did.

lines.japanese: 二階へ上がると、まっすぐ自分の部屋へ向かった。
lines.english: Upstairs, I went directly to my room.

lines.japanese: きのうのニュースは気になるけれど、その話題は朝すでに使ってしまったし、冷静に考えれば家族の誰かに聞くよりネットで調べた方が早くて確実だ。
lines.english: Yesterday's news still interested me, but I had already used that subject this morning. Considered calmly, looking it up online would be faster and more reliable than asking someone in the family.

lines.japanese: こうして世界中の家庭から団欒の時間が削られてゆくのだとしたら、これもまたＩＴ時代のもたらした弊害のひとつと言っていいだろう。
lines.english: If this was how households throughout the world were losing their time together, one could fairly call it another evil of the information age.

lines.japanese: 押しよせる情報の波が、今日も僕を妹から引きはなす。
lines.english: Once again, the onrushing tide of information bore me away from my sister.

lines.japanese: その後、入浴と食事をさっさと済ませた。
lines.english: I made quick work of my bath and dinner.

lines.japanese: 自室へ戻ってきた僕は、生乾きの髪に適当な手櫛を通しながらパソコンに向かった。
lines.english: Back in my room, I faced the computer and raked careless fingers through my half-dry hair.

lines.japanese: 起動したあとはまず音楽をかけて、メールをチェックして、溜息をついて、そうだテストも終わったことだし久々にゆっくりオンラインＲＰＧでもやろうかと思って、でもやっぱり気が乗らないで──
lines.english: Once it booted, I put on some music, checked my email, sighed, remembered the exams were over and thought I might finally settle into an online role-playing game for the first time in ages, then found I was not in the mood after all—

lines.japanese: ──とりあえずブックマークしてあるサイトのいくつかを巡回した。
lines.english: —and settled for making the rounds of a few bookmarked sites.

lines.japanese: 優先順位の低い『鷹は舞いおりた』へ辿りついたのは、午前１時を過ぎたあとだった。
lines.english: It was past one in the morning when I finally reached the low-priority site *The Hawk Has Landed*.

lines.japanese: どんよりした効果音やホラーゲームの洋館みたいなデザインをすり抜けて、トップページから創作掲示板まで潜っていく。
lines.english: I slipped past the gloomy sound effects and a design straight out of a mansion in a horror game, descending from the front page to the creative-writing board.

lines.japanese: 黒地に単一フレームというアナクロな構成。いちばん上に、ゆうべ見たルカ君の作品がある。欠伸しながらホイールを回せば、下からせり上がってくるのは２７時間前に僕が付けたレスだ。
lines.english: A black background and a single frame: an anachronism in website form. At the top was the work by Ruka I had read the night before. I yawned and spun the wheel, bringing up from below the reply I had posted twenty-seven hours earlier.

lines.japanese: ちょっと恥ずかしくなって回転速度を上げると、意外なことに、昨晩はそこで終わっていたはずのスレッドが新しい書き込みによって少しだけ延びていた。
lines.english: A little embarrassed, I scrolled faster. To my surprise, the thread that had ended there last night had grown by one new post.

lines.japanese: 『投稿者：瑠樺』
lines.english: “Posted by: Ruka”

lines.japanese: ルカ君本人からのレスポンスだった。投稿時刻は朝の５時過ぎ、僕の書き込みから数時間後だ。
lines.english: It was a response from Ruka himself, posted just after five that morning, a few hours after mine.

lines.japanese: 僕は太ももに手を置き、前傾姿勢でディスプレイへ近づいた。
lines.english: I placed a hand on my thigh and leaned toward the display.

lines.japanese: 『題名：ありがとう～もしくは、それをまっすぐ伝えるにはちょっと照れくさい僕なりの返歌～』
lines.english: “Title: Thank You—or, My Answer in Verse, Since Saying It Straight Would Embarrass Me”

lines.japanese: 『格子の向こうの動物たちは今日も元気に痛ましかった』
lines.english: “Behind the bars, the animals were lively and pitiful as ever today.”

lines.japanese: 『鳴きわめく駱駝に声をかけよう』
lines.english: “Call out to the camel crying itself hoarse.”

lines.japanese: 『乾きそうな海驢に水をかけよう』
lines.english: “Splash water on the sea lion about to dry out.”

lines.japanese: 『溺れそうな陸亀に情けをかけよう』
lines.english: “Show mercy to the land tortoise about to drown.”

lines.japanese: 『格子の向こうの動物たちは今日も元気に捻くれていた』
lines.english: “Behind the bars, the animals were lively and twisted as ever today.”

lines.japanese: 『駱駝は言った“ありがとうそんな高いところから”』
lines.english: “The camel said, ‘Thank you, from all the way up there.’”

lines.japanese: 『海驢は言った“ありがとうまるで自分を慰めるように”』
lines.english: “The sea lion said, ‘Thank you, as though you were comforting yourself.’”

lines.japanese: 『陸亀は言った“ありがとう寂しがり屋の禿鷹さん”』
lines.english: “The tortoise said, ‘Thank you, you lonely vulture.’”

lines.japanese: 『みんなで言った“ところでそっちの檻は快適かい？”』
lines.english: “Together they said, ‘By the way, is your own cage comfortable?’”

lines.japanese: 『追記：エビ塩とんこつラーメンは近日中に試してみる。僕が勧めるのは隣りのカフェのチキンフィレサンドだ。機会があれば挑んでくれ』
lines.english: “P.S. I'll try the shrimp-and-salt pork-broth ramen soon. My recommendation is the chicken fillet sandwich at the café next door. Give it a try if you get the chance.”

lines.japanese: 目を通しおえた僕は、鼻から細い息を吹きながらゆっくり頭を引いた。
lines.english: When I finished reading, I let a thin breath out through my nose and slowly drew back.

lines.japanese: これは……なんて言うか、その、なんて言えばいいんだろう。
lines.english: This was... Well, what could I say? How was I supposed to put it?

lines.japanese: 彼の言いたいことが伝わって来るような来ないような……。
lines.english: It felt as though I understood what he wanted to say, and as though I did not...

lines.japanese: 僕は腕を組んでしばし考えてからキーボードを叩いた。
lines.english: I folded my arms and considered for a while, then began to type.

lines.japanese: 『投稿者：汰架示』
lines.english: “Posted by: Takashi”

lines.japanese: 『題名：無題』
lines.english: “Title: Untitled”

lines.japanese: 『禿鷹は答えた“こっちの檻は広いけれど翼の折れたオイラにゃ関係のない話さ”』
lines.english: “The vulture answered, ‘My cage is spacious, but what does that matter to a bird with broken wings?’”

lines.japanese: 『追記：僕らはいつかモンキホーテ柳木原店の地下で擦れちがうかもしれない（笑）』
lines.english: “P.S. Someday we may pass each other in the basement of Monki Hote's Yanagihara branch. (laugh)”

lines.japanese: 「送、信、っと……」
lines.english: “And... send.”

lines.japanese: 画面が切りかわり「投稿しました」の文字が出た。僕は小さな達成感に息をついた。
lines.english: The screen changed, and the words “Your post has been submitted” appeared. I breathed out with a small sense of accomplishment.

lines.japanese: それから巡回ルートの残りをだらだら消化して、メールチェックして、溜息をついて、プレイ途中の恋愛ゲームでも始めようかと思って、でもやっぱり眠くなってきたので電気を消して布団に入って目を閉じた。
lines.english: Then I idled through the rest of my usual rounds, checked my email, sighed, thought about returning to the dating game I had left unfinished, and found myself growing sleepy after all. I turned off the light, climbed into bed, and closed my eyes.

lines.japanese: よほど疲れていたのか、その夜はぐっすり眠れた。
lines.english: I must have been exhausted. That night I slept soundly.

lines.japanese: たったそれだけのことが、生まれつき浅い眠りが多く、慢性的な睡眠不足に悩まされている僕にはとても有難いことだった。
lines.english: For someone born a light sleeper and plagued by chronic sleep deprivation, that simple fact was an enormous blessing.

lines.japanese: とくに夢は見なかった。
lines.english: I had no dreams to speak of.
